items.text: This Comedian Was Called Out For A Transphobic Joke. Then She Did The Unexpected.
items.article: For years, we’ve watched famous comedians turn criticism over a single joke into an existential battle about whether comedy is allowed to exist. It’s no secret that trans people in America are under attack — so much so that some organizations have expressed that the unrelenting patterns of violence against them resemble the beginning stages of a genocide. That might sound extreme until you examine both individual and systemic anti-trans events over the past few years. More than 100 state laws targeting transgender rights have passed since 2020 , according to the American Civil Liberties Union, while trans people have increasingly become the obsession of politicians and right-wing activists. For this reason, making jokes at the expense of trans people right now is no laughing matter, but that hasn’t stopped some of the biggest names in comedy from doubling down. Two examples in modern pop history include Dave Chappelle, whose jokes about trans people have generated controversy for years, and Ricky Gervais, who devoted portions of his 2022 Netflix special “SuperNature” to jokes about trans women. He later brushed off the criticism by saying that “comedy exists to explore taboo subjects .” After backlash to these jokes, they both expressed their right to creative freedom and argued that the nature of stand-up will always be to “push the envelope.” But a recent controversy involving Nikki Glaser showed that there is another option: You can simply acknowledge when a joke missed
